An air removal assembly is configured for use with a fluid system and includes an air valve that is mountable on the fluid system. The air valve is arranged to remove air from the fluid system during operation.

The assembly further includes a throttling device that is in fluid communication with the air valve. Through the air valve, the throttling device is also in fluid communication with the fluid system. In this arrangement, fluid and/or air from the fluid system may pass through the air valve and into or through the throttling device.

The throttling device includes a body having an inner surface and an outer surface. The inner surface defines a body cavity within the body, while the body also includes a plurality of body orifices that provide fluid communication between the body cavity and regions outside the body.

A movable throttle is positioned within the body cavity. The throttle is located near a first orifice of the plurality of body orifices and is configured to move relative to the body. In particular, the throttle is movable between a closed position, in which flow through the first orifice is restricted or prevented, and an open position, in which flow through the first orifice is permitted.

The throttling device also includes a biasing element that engages or otherwise acts on the movable throttle. The biasing element biases the throttle toward a partially open position located between the closed position and the open position. As a result, the throttle may normally remain partially open while still being capable of moving toward either the closed position or the open position in response to operating conditions within the air removal assembly.
outputs.L4:
An air removal assembly is provided for use in a fluid system in which it is desirable to discharge trapped air while regulating the flow of fluid through the assembly. The assembly includes an air valve coupled to a throttling device. The throttling device is configured to control communication between the fluid system and the air valve so that air may be removed from the system in a controlled manner while reducing the likelihood of excessive fluid discharge.

The throttling device includes a body defining an internal cavity. A plurality of orifices are formed in the body and communicate with the cavity to permit air, fluid, or a mixture of air and fluid to pass through the device. A movable throttle is positioned within or adjacent to the cavity and is arranged to move relative to the orifices. The throttle may be displaced between different operating positions to vary the amount of flow permitted through the throttling device.

In one operating position, the throttle may be located in a closed position in which flow through one or more of the orifices is substantially blocked. In another operating position, the throttle may be moved to an open position in which the orifices are substantially unobstructed, allowing a greater volume of air or fluid to pass through the assembly. The throttle may also assume one or more intermediate or partially open positions. In these partially open positions, the throttle restricts flow through the orifices to a controlled degree, thereby permitting gradual or regulated discharge from the fluid system.

A biasing element, such as a spring or other resilient member, is operatively associated with the throttle. The biasing element urges the throttle toward a predetermined position, such as the closed position, the open position, or an intermediate position, depending on the desired operating characteristics of the assembly. Fluid pressure, air pressure, buoyancy, or other forces within the system may act against the biasing force to shift the throttle from one position to another.

During operation, air accumulating in the fluid system is directed toward the air removal assembly. As air enters the throttling device, the throttle may move to permit air to pass through the cavity and the orifices to the air valve. The air valve then vents the air from the system. When liquid reaches the assembly, the throttle may shift toward a more restricted or closed position to limit the flow of liquid. This helps prevent sudden discharge, reduces fluid loss, and allows the air valve to operate more effectively.

The use of multiple orifices and a movable throttle provides improved control over the venting process. Rather than allowing unrestricted flow at all times, the assembly can respond to changing conditions within the fluid system. For example, the throttle may open widely when a large volume of air is present, partially close when a mixture of air and fluid is passing through the device, and close or substantially close when liquid flow predominates. This staged or variable response improves air removal regulation and may enhance the overall performance and reliability of the fluid system.

The air removal assembly may be used in a variety of fluid systems, including piping networks, heating and cooling systems, irrigation systems, pumping systems, hydraulic circuits, and other installations where trapped air can interfere with performance. By combining an air valve with a throttling device having a cavity, multiple orifices, a movable throttle, and a biasing element, the assembly provides a compact and effective mechanism for controlled air discharge and fluid flow regulation.
outputs.L5:
**An Air Removal**

An air removal is an important process used in many systems to eliminate trapped air and improve performance. Air can enter pipes, heating systems, pumps, or other equipment and cause problems such as noise, reduced efficiency, corrosion, or poor circulation. By removing air, the system can operate more smoothly and safely.

In heating and plumbing systems, an air removal device helps release air pockets that build up over time. These air pockets can block the flow of water and make the system less effective. Regular air removal can help prevent damage and extend the life of the equipment.

An air removal process is also used in industrial applications, medical devices, and manufacturing. In each case, removing unwanted air helps maintain quality, pressure, and proper function. Whether it is done manually or with an automatic air removal valve, the goal is to keep the system free from trapped air and working efficiently.

Below is sample patent claim language for an invention involving an air valve connected to a fluid system and a throttling device having a body cavity, body orifices, a movable throttle, and a biasing element. This is drafting-style language and should be reviewed by patent counsel for suitability, scope, and jurisdictional requirements.

## Claims

### 1. Independent Apparatus Claim

1. **A fluid control assembly**, comprising:  
   an air valve configured to be fluidly connected to a fluid system; and  
   a throttling device fluidly coupled to the air valve, the throttling device comprising:  
   a body defining a body cavity;  
   a plurality of body orifices extending through the body and providing fluid communication between the body cavity and the fluid system;  
   a movable throttle disposed at least partially within the body cavity and movable relative to the plurality of body orifices between a first position and a second position to vary a flow area through at least one of the plurality of body orifices; and  
   a biasing element arranged to bias the movable throttle toward the first position.

### 2. Dependent Claims

2. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the air valve is configured to vent air from the fluid system.

3. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the air valve is configured to admit air into the fluid system.

4. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the air valve is a combination air-release and vacuum-relief valve.

5. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable throttle is movable in response to a pressure differential across the throttling device.

6. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable throttle comprises a piston.

7. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable throttle comprises a sleeve configured to selectively cover and uncover at least one of the plurality of body orifices.

8. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable throttle includes at least one throttle opening configured to align with at least one of the plurality of body orifices in at least one position of the movable throttle.

9. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein movement of the movable throttle from the first position toward the second position progressively reduces an effective flow area through the plurality of body orifices.

10. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein movement of the movable throttle from the first position toward the second position progressively increases an effective flow area through the plurality of body orifices.

11. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the biasing element comprises a spring.

12. The fluid control assembly of claim 11, wherein the spring is a compression spring positioned in the body cavity.

13. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the biasing element is positioned between the movable throttle and an internal surface of the body.

14. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the body comprises an inlet end and an outlet end, and wherein the plurality of body orifices are circumferentially spaced around the body.

15. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the plurality of body orifices includes a first set of orifices and a second set of orifices having different sizes.

16. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable throttle is configured to dampen rapid changes in fluid flow through the air valve.

17. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the throttling device is disposed between the air valve and the fluid system.

18. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the throttling device is integrally formed with a housing of the air valve.

19. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the throttling device is removably coupled to the air valve.

20. The fluid control assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable throttle is configured to move against a force of the biasing element when fluid flow through the throttling device exceeds a threshold flow condition.

---

### 3. Alternative Independent Apparatus Claim

21. **An air valve assembly for a fluid system**, comprising:  
   an air valve having a valve inlet configured for connection to the fluid system and a valve outlet configured to discharge or receive air; and  
   a throttling device positioned in a flow path between the valve inlet and the fluid system, the throttling device including:  
   a housing defining an internal cavity;  
   a plurality of openings formed through the housing;  
   a throttle member received in the internal cavity and movable relative to the plurality of openings to selectively restrict fluid flow through the openings; and  
   a spring configured to urge the throttle member toward an unthrottled position;  
   wherein the throttle member is configured to move from the unthrottled position toward a throttled position in response to fluid flow through the throttling device.

### 4. Dependent Claims for Alternative Embodiments

22. The air valve assembly of claim 21, wherein the throttle member is axially movable within the internal cavity.

23. The air valve assembly of claim 21, wherein the throttle member is rotatable within the internal cavity.

24. The air valve assembly of claim 21, wherein the throttle member includes a cylindrical wall configured to overlap the plurality of openings.

25. The air valve assembly of claim 21, wherein the spring force is selected to permit movement of the throttle member only when a predetermined pressure differential is exceeded.

26. The air valve assembly of claim 21, wherein the throttling device limits discharge of fluid through the air valve during closure of the air valve.

27. The air valve assembly of claim 21, wherein the throttling device limits intake of air through the air valve during draining of the fluid system.

28. The air valve assembly of claim 21, wherein the throttle member includes a sealing surface configured to engage a seat in the housing.

29. The air valve assembly of claim 21, wherein the plurality of openings are arranged to provide staged throttling as the throttle member moves.

30. The air valve assembly of claim 21, wherein the throttling device is configured to reduce water hammer in the fluid system.

---

### 5. Method Claim

31. **A method of controlling flow through an air valve connected to a fluid system**, comprising:  
   directing fluid or air through a throttling device coupled between the air valve and the fluid system, the throttling device having a body cavity and a plurality of body orifices;  
   moving a throttle within the body cavity relative to the plurality of body orifices in response to a flow condition through the throttling device;  
   varying an effective flow area through at least one of the plurality of body orifices by the movement of the throttle; and  
   biasing the throttle toward a default position with a biasing element.

32. The method of claim 31, further comprising moving the throttle against a spring force when a pressure differential across the throttling device exceeds a predetermined value.

33. The method of claim 31, further comprising progressively restricting flow through the plurality of body orifices as flow through the throttling device increases.

34. The method of claim 31, further comprising returning the throttle toward the default position when the flow condition decreases below a threshold.

35. The method of claim 31, wherein varying the effective flow area comprises covering or uncovering at least one of the plurality of body orifices with the throttle.

---

### 6. Broad Independent Claim

36. **A throttled air valve system**, comprising:  
   a fluid-system connection;  
   an air valve in fluid communication with the fluid-system connection; and  
   a flow-responsive throttling mechanism arranged between the fluid-system connection and the air valve, the flow-responsive throttling mechanism comprising a cavity, a plurality of flow orifices, a throttle element movable relative to the plurality of flow orifices, and a resilient biasing member configured to urge the throttle element toward a rest position,  
   wherein movement of the throttle element changes a total available flow area through the plurality of flow orifices to regulate flow between the fluid system and the air valve.
